title: UMich vs UMN: tuition, size, location
summary: University of Michigan-Ann Arbor (UMich) versus University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN). Also searched as UMN vs UMich. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: The University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN) and the University of Michigan-Ann Arbor (UMich) are both public institutions located in major Midwestern cities, Minneapolis and Ann Arbor respectively. UMN has an undergraduate enrollment of 31,855 students, slightly fewer than UMich's 34,177 undergraduates. In-state tuition at UMN is $17,214, which is marginally lower than UMich's $17,736. These differences reflect variations in size and cost between the two universities, despite their similar public status and regional proximity.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing the cost of attendance, the University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN) and the University of Michigan-Ann Arbor (UMich) show notable differences, especially for out-of-state students. UMN charges $17,214 for in-state tuition, slightly less than UMich's $17,736. However, out-of-state tuition at UMN is $38,362, significantly lower than UMich's $60,946. Both universities report the same median debt for degree completers, which is $19,500. These figures highlight that while in-state tuition costs are comparable, UMN offers a more affordable option for out-of-state students compared to UMich.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: The University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN) and the University of Michigan-Ann Arbor (UMich) both employ traditional learning models with a focus on in-person instruction complemented by online resources. UMN is situated in Minneapolis, Minnesota, while UMich is located in Ann Arbor, Michigan. The undergraduate enrollment at UMN is 31,855, which is slightly less than UMich's 34,177 students. Both campuses are urban and provide extensive facilities to support a diverse range of academic programs and student activities. Comparing UMN vs UMich, the differences in undergraduate population and campus settings reflect their unique regional characteristics and institutional priorities.

sections.heading: Accreditation
paragraphs: The University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN) and the University of Michigan-Ann Arbor (UMich) are both accredited institutions, ensuring that they meet established standards of quality in higher education. Accreditation supports the recognition of their academic programs and facilitates credit transfer and eligibility for federal funding. While specific accrediting bodies are not detailed here, both UMN and UMich maintain accreditation status that reflects their commitment to academic excellence and institutional integrity.

sections.heading: Pick UMN if
paragraphs: Pick the University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN) if you prefer a public university with a higher admission rate, as UMN admits approximately 79.75% of applicants compared to many selective institutions. UMN offers in-state tuition at $17,214, which is a cost-effective option for Minnesota residents. Additionally, UMN has a strong completion rate, with about 85.28% of students finishing their degrees within 150% of the expected time. When comparing UMN vs UMich, these factors make UMN a suitable choice for students seeking accessible admission, reasonable in-state tuition, and a high likelihood of degree completion.

sections.heading: Pick UMich if
paragraphs: Pick the University of Michigan-Ann Arbor (UMich) if you are looking for a highly selective public university with an admission rate of about 15.64%. UMich charges in-state tuition of $17,736, which is slightly higher than the University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN). The completion rate at UMich is notably high, with approximately 93.2% of students finishing their degrees within 150% of the expected time. When comparing UMN vs UMich, UMich stands out for its selectivity and strong student success in degree completion.
